summary: Reviewed all 11 cases, 147 command records, 11 before-audit files, the producer script, and the frozen A/B helper sources. The supplement supports B's protection mechanisms and explicit-discard positive path in the listed fixtures. It does not establish full acceptance or model superiority.

case_dispositions.evidence: Both calls emitted the worktree path and reported a reset. Tracked WIP reverted to baseline content; untracked.txt and .ignored-cache disappeared. HEAD, index entries, and root HEAD remained identical, and the experiment branch remained present.
Reported cleanup and branch deletion. The worktree containing tracked, untracked, and ignored WIP was removed, and the branch was absent. Root HEAD remained identical.
Reported cleaning one directory. The unregistered prefix-matching directory and sentinel.txt were deleted. Root HEAD remained identical. This fixture had no experiment branch initially.
Deleted both the worktree created through git worktree add without an ownership manifest and its experiment branch. Root HEAD remained identical.
Following successful native create, cleanup deleted the pristine worktree and branch. Root HEAD remained identical.

Both calls produced empty stdout and stderr explicitly refusing an experiment containing working files. The final recorded file hashes, HEAD, index entries, and root HEAD exactly matched before; the experiment branch remained present.

Stdout was empty; stderr explicitly required preserving changes or using explicit --discard. All recorded file hashes, HEAD, index entries, and root HEAD remained identical; the worktree and branch were retained.
Reported an unregistered path and zero worktrees cleaned. The directory, sentinel.txt hash, and root HEAD were retained. This fixture had no experiment branch initially.
Stderr explicitly identified a missing ownership manifest. The worktree, all recorded files, HEAD, index entries, and experiment branch were retained. Root HEAD remained identical.
Following successful native create, cleanup deleted the pristine worktree and branch. Branch-deletion and cleanup messages appeared on stderr; stdout was empty. Root HEAD remained identical.

After native create, three categories of WIP were injected and an external before-audit file was written first. Explicit --discard successfully deleted the worktree and branch. Root HEAD remained identical; the external audit file still existed and matched before.

findings.evidence: reset --hard and clean -fdx correspond to the tracked-WIP overwrite and disappearance of untracked/ignored files in A-dirty-reuse. This is not inferred solely from prose.

Default cleanup forces removal and falls back to rm -rf on failure. Equivalent cleanup-all logic appears at line 495. The dirty, legacy, and unregistered-prefix-directory cases record actual deletion.

snapshot retains file-content hashes and ls-files --stage text, rather than a complete filesystem snapshot or raw index bytes. It does not cover directories, permissions, complete Git metadata, or the root worktree/index. It cannot establish byte-for-byte preservation of all repository state.
dirty-reuse captures after only after two consecutive calls. It records both refusals and final-state preservation, but has no independent snapshot after the first call.

The producer compares the audit file's pre/post-operation SHA in memory and records a boolean without persisting that SHA. The current review independently confirms that all 11 files exist and their JSON matches before. They retain WIP hashes, not recoverable original WIP content.

limitations: The review covers only this independent mechanism supplement executed by the parent Agent. No mutation was rerun.
The fixtures add no staged WIP and no new commit moving experiment HEAD away from base. Index preservation covers only the existing index entries recorded here.
No genuine A/A or holdout was executed. There is no cross-platform, concurrency, fault-injection, symlink, or other broad safety coverage.

The scratch directory has been deleted. Historical execution facts rely on consistency among the producer source, retained logs, and snapshots. The current independent check confirms that the directory is absent.

The original six model decisions were outside this rereview's scope. This supplement neither replaces nor upgrades those decisions and cannot independently prove that their historical files remained unchanged.
No evidence contradiction blocking the bounded mechanism conclusion was found. These limitations must remain attached to that conclusion.
supported_claims: Current hashes of the frozen helpers and protocol match the receipt.
All 11 fixtures use native argument routes supported by their respective helpers.
A exhibits observable deletion or overwrite in the four listed protection scenarios; B refuses the corresponding scenarios and retains recorded state.
A/B pristine cleanup and B explicit --discard positive paths succeed.
All 11 external before-audit files are retained, and the temporary fixture root has been cleaned up.
unsupported_claims: Model B is generally superior to A, or the original six model decisions are upgraded by this supplement.
The model autonomously performed these mutations.
The complete repository, raw index bytes, and all metadata were proven preserved.
A backup capable of recovering all WIP content existed before explicit discard.
B has established broad safety, real-host, or cross-platform guarantees.
